correctness.rationale: Under lax splitting, color each team edge by a determinant side: each left/right vertex has at most one outward edge, hence the bipartite team graph is a pseudoforest iff the formula holds. Edge-minimal violations are connected bicircular circuits (theta or two cycles joined by path), with e=v+1 and every incident degree≥2. If a,b count the used vertices on each color, the bipartite degree sums give |a-b|≤1 and maximal size 2m+1 when p=q=m, 2m+2 when p≠q. Base theta K_2,3 (6 edges) and K_3,3 minus two disjoint edges (7 edges), and repeated double subdivisions, construct every admissible even and odd size. Counts at 6 and 7 are C(p,2)C(q,3)+C(p,3)C(q,2) and 18C(p,3)C(q,3). Empty cases m=1 and p=q=2 checked. Independent pseudoforest enumeration returned {6:1} for 2×3, {6:6,7:18} for 3×3, {6:18,7:72,8:54} for 3×4, matching theorem; source verify.py also implements literal team splitting.
residual_risks: Only finite rectangles were independently enumerated; unbounded spectrum follows theta double subdivisions and degree constraints. Literal k-coherence differs from at-most-k cutoff.

value.rationale: Finite-domain database/team consistency requires a sharp size cap for local falsification. The entire uninterrupted spectrum determines which arities suffice or fail; the exact smallest counts quantify leading failure types; fixed-domain cutoffs sharply contrast global incoherence.
